newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trade on Monday with many investors reluctant to hold positions during the approaching Labour Day holiday, traders said.
Shanghai Cereals and Oils Exchange will suspend trading in soybeans on May 1 and 2, resuming next Monday, exchange officials said.
The most actively traded July 1997 contract ended at 3,320 yuan ($400) per tonne, losing 11 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 3,300 yuan per tonne and hit a high of 3,331 yuan.
May did not trade, September fell five yuan to 3,391, November rose 40 to 3,400, the January 1998 contract rose five to 3,410 and the May 1998 contract 15 to 3,390.
Combined volume fell sharply to 9,800 tonnes from 23,200.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved around opening levels for most of the session, traders said. "Most investors prefer to stay on the sidelines with the approach of the holiday," one trader said.
"A lack of market-moving news also dampened investors' interest in trading," he said. ($1=8.2955 yuan)
